description: Get perpetual funding rates across every supported venue (see sharpe://exchanges for the current list). Returns current snapshots, accumulated rates over multiple windows, or per-coin historical rates. Units: `rate` is a decimal fraction settled over that row's own `interval_hours` (1h, 2h, 4h, 8h or 24h depending on venue and market). It is not a percent and never implicitly 8h. On most venues `rate` is the in-progress estimate for the coming settlement, not what was last charged; `rate_kind` says which (`estimate`, `last_settled` on Kraken/Crypto.com/Bitfinex, `trailing_8h` on Deribit), and type=history serves the settled rates. Compare or rank venues on the served rate_8h (rate × 8 / interval_hours) or apr (rate × 8760 / interval_hours), both null when the row has no usable interval. Accumulated rows carry realized sums (acc_1d/acc_7d/acc_30d/acc_90d/acc_1y) instead of a per-interval rate, each annualised over the history behind it (acc_apr_1d … acc_apr_1y), and per window a `coverage` entry (coverage_ratio, complete, listed_within_window, halted_within_window): compare acc_* across contracts only on complete windows where listed_within_window and halted_within_window are both false. Filter with coin, exchange, margin (linear/inverse) and asset_class; asset_class is unfiltered by default, so tokenized-equity, commodity, index and FX perps are included alongside crypto. `coin` names an asset: PEPE returns every PEPE contract, the 1000PEPE and KPEPE lot contracts included. Current and accumulated rows carry asset_id, asset_symbol, lot_multiplier (asset units per contract unit, e.g. 1000 on 1000PEPEUSDT), instrument_status (the venue's own status) and is_live (null = unknown). Page the full book with limit and cursor, or order it by open interest with sort. For type=current the API also answers with aggregates instead of rows: extremes (the highest and lowest markets by rate_8h above an optional min_oi_usd floor), stats (the whole book's mean and OI-weighted funding APR, the positive/negative counts, and venue_count/live_venues) and summary (with coin: the coin's average and median funding across venues, the funding grid's Avg Rate, its open interest over every contract and its next settlement). With type=accumulated, coin and summary=1 it answers per window the median realised funding and median APR over the venues whose history covers the window, and the carry spread APR (best short venue minus best long venue).

asset_class.description: Narrow the response to one underlying category. The funding book is not crypto-only. Tokenized equity, commodity, index and FX perps trade on the same venues, so this is unfiltered by default. Applies to type=current and type=accumulated; ignored for type=history. An unrecognized value returns 400.

coin.description: The coin to return: a ticker (e.g. BTC), a lot or venue spelling (e.g. `1000PEPE`, `kPEPE`), or the full name (e.g. `bitcoin`, resolved to BTC). Case-insensitive, one coin per request. `coin` names an asset, not a base_coin string: every contract of that asset is returned whatever its base_coin spelling, so `PEPE` also returns the 1000PEPE and KPEPE lot contracts (read `lot_multiplier`), and a ticker two assets share (BB is BounceBit and BlackBerry) returns both, narrowed by `asset_class`. Optional filter for type=current and type=accumulated; required when type=history. A value that no perpetual in the funding book has ever settled returns 400 rather than an empty result set; GET /api/funding/coins lists every ticker carried.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

days.description: Number of days of history to retrieve (type=history only).

exchange.description: Filter to a single venue. Accepts the slug (e.g. `gate-io`), the display name as returned in the `exchange` field (e.g. `Gate.io`), or the ccxt id. The venue registry is not frozen, so read the `sharpe://exchanges` MCP resource or /api/funding/rates for the current list. An unrecognized value returns 400.

extremes.description: type=current only: answer with the N highest and N lowest rows by `rate_8h` (`extremes.highest`, `extremes.lowest`) among fresh rows with a usable interval, and how many rows each check left out (`extremes.omitted`). The other filters narrow the rows first. Returns an object instead of rows; cannot be combined with `limit`, `cursor` or `sort`.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page.

margin.description: Narrow the response to one collateral convention: `linear` for quote-margined contracts, `inverse` for coin-margined ones. Unfiltered by default. Applies to type=current and type=accumulated; ignored for type=history. An unrecognized value returns 400.

min_oi_usd.description: type=current, with `extremes` only: leave out rows whose open interest in USD is below this floor. A row with unknown open interest fails a floor above 0.

sort.description: type=current only: order the rows by `open_interest`, ascending, or descending with the leading `-`. Rows with unknown open interest come last either way. Applied before `limit`/`cursor`. Default: the book's order (base_coin, exchange, symbol).

stats.description: type=current only: `1` answers with the whole book's funding (`market`: mean and open-interest-weighted APR, the count of positive and negative rates, and how many of the tracked venues have a fresh contract). Returns an object instead of rows; cannot be combined with `coin`, `exchange`, `margin`, `asset_class`, `limit`, `cursor` or `sort`.

summary.description: type=current or type=accumulated, with `coin` only: `1` answers with the coin's funding across venues (`summary`) instead of the rows. For type=current: the average and median 8-hour rate, how they were reduced, the venues behind them, the open interest of every contract and the next settlement. For type=accumulated, per window: the median realised funding and the median APR over the venues whose history covers the window, and the carry spread APR (best short venue minus best long venue). Returns an object instead of rows; cannot be combined with `limit`, `cursor` or `sort`.

type.description: Type of funding rate data to retrieve.

name: get_funding_rates

asset_class.description: Underlying category, joined in from the live contract book. `null` when no live contract matches, rather than being defaulted to `crypto`.

asset_id.description: The instrument master asset of this contract: the CoinGecko id when the asset was resolved strictly (`pepe`), otherwise `<class>:<ticker>` (`equity:bb`). Every contract of one asset carries the same id, whatever its base_coin spelling. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

asset_symbol.description: The asset ticker as a trader reads it: `PEPE` on the 1000PEPE and KPEPE contracts too. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

coverage.description: How much of each window (`acc_1d` … `acc_1y`) the contract's settlements cover, judged against when it was listed and when it stopped trading.

covered_hours_1d.description: Hours of funding the settlements summed in `acc_1d` stand for: the sum of their `interval_hours`. Fewer hours than the window (or than the contract's listed span inside it) means missing settlements, also in the middle of the window. It can exceed the window by up to one interval (a first settlement's interval reaches back past the window start). `null` when unknown.

covered_hours_1y.description: Hours of funding the settlements summed in `acc_1y` stand for: the sum of their `interval_hours`. Fewer hours than the window (or than the contract's listed span inside it) means missing settlements, also in the middle of the window. It can exceed the window by up to one interval (a first settlement's interval reaches back past the window start). `null` when unknown.

covered_hours_30d.description: Hours of funding the settlements summed in `acc_30d` stand for: the sum of their `interval_hours`. It can exceed the window by up to one interval (a first settlement's interval reaches back past the window start). `null` when unknown.

It can exceed the window by up to one interval (a first settlement's interval reaches back past the window start). `null` when unknown.

covered_hours_90d.description: Hours of funding the settlements summed in `acc_90d` stand for: the sum of their `interval_hours`. Fewer hours than the window (or than the contract's listed span inside it) means missing settlements, also in the middle of the window. It can exceed the window by up to one interval (a first settlement's interval reaches back past the window start). `null` when unknown.

instrument_status.description: The venue's own status for the contract, as the instruments sync last read it. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

is_active.description: `false` when the accumulated identity has no live contract behind it, meaning a delisted or renamed pair. Those rows keep their accumulated history but carry `null` metadata.

is_live.description: `true`: trading, and the venue's contract list was read within 30 minutes. `false`: read within 30 minutes and not trading. `null`: unknown (no read in 30 minutes, a status value the sync could not interpret, or a contract the master does not know).

lot_multiplier.description: Units of the asset per unit the contract quotes: `1000` for Binance 1000PEPEUSDT, `1` for Gate.io PEPE_USDT. From the venue or a checked alias, never parsed from the symbol. `rate` is a fraction of notional and needs no scaling. `null` when unknown.

margin_type.description: Collateral convention, joined in from the live contract book. `null` when no live contract matches.

base_coin.description: The entry's ticker: the coin's asset_symbol when the instrument master knows it, else the underlying ticker, as on the type=current summary.

asset_id.description: The instrument master's CoinGecko id the entry groups by (`pepe`), or `null` when it groups by ticker (non-crypto assets, and coins the master has not placed). Two coins can share a ticker (MEME is both `memecoin-2` and `a-meme-coin`): `asset_id` tells their entries apart.

base_coin.description: The group's ticker: the coin's asset_symbol when the instrument master knows it, else the underlying ticker. Groups follow the funding grid: one per instrument and asset class, so `coin=PEPE` answers one `PEPE` entry over the PEPE, 1000PEPE and KPEPE contracts, KOSTOCK and NCSKKO2USD join KO, and a ticker two asset classes share answers one entry per class.

funding_all_stale.description: `true` when no venue was fresh: the figures are then over the stale rates, and read as such.

funding_median_8h.description: Median of the same venues' 8-hour rates: the companion one venue cannot move.

funding_method.description: How `funding_avg_8h` was reduced: `oi_weighted`, or `median_fallback` when too few venues carry open interest. `null` with `funding_avg_8h`.

funding_venues_stale.description: Venues left out because their rate was past the 10-minute freshness SLA, or was a `trailing_8h` rate (Deribit), while another venue was fresh.

funding_venues_used.description: Venues behind the figures, one primary contract each.

asset_class.description: Underlying category: `crypto`, `equity`, `commodity`, `fx` or `index`. Tokenized-equity perps such as Bybit `TSLL` are `equity`, not `crypto`.

asset_id.description: The instrument master asset of this contract: the CoinGecko id when the asset was resolved strictly (`pepe`), otherwise `<class>:<ticker>` (`equity:bb`). Every contract of one asset carries the same id, whatever its base_coin spelling. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

asset_symbol.description: The asset ticker as a trader reads it: `PEPE` on the 1000PEPE and KPEPE contracts too. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

instrument_status.description: The venue's own status for the contract, as the instruments sync last read it. `null` when the master does not know the contract.

is_live.description: `true`: trading, and the venue's contract list was read within 30 minutes. `false`: read within 30 minutes and not trading. `null`: unknown (no read in 30 minutes, a status value the sync could not interpret, or a contract the master does not know).

lot_multiplier.description: Units of the asset per unit the contract quotes: `1000` for Binance 1000PEPEUSDT, `1` for Gate.io PEPE_USDT. From the venue or a checked alias, never parsed from the symbol. `rate` is a fraction of notional and needs no scaling. `null` when unknown.

margin_type.description: Collateral convention for the contract: `linear` (quote-margined) or `inverse` (coin-margined).

mark_price.description: Binance's mark price for the base coin (from its premiumIndex feed), attached to every venue's row for that coin as context: it is not this venue's own mark or a traded quote. A lot contract such as `1000PEPE` carries Binance's lot price as is; a bare coin that Binance lists only as a lot is priced at the lot price divided by the lot size. `null` when Binance has no contract for the coin in the same asset class.

market_cap_rank.description: Market-cap rank of the base coin, where `1` is the largest. `null` when the coin is unranked. Sort unranked rows last rather than treating `null` as a rank.

predicted_rate.description: The venue's own forecast for the coming settlement, when it publishes one beside `rate`: Kraken (`fundingRatePrediction`), Crypto.com (`estimated_funding_rate`, an estimate for the next 4-hour interval rather than the next hourly settlement), Pacifica (`next_funding_rate`), and Hyperliquid, where it is a copy of `rate`. `null` on every other venue (about 93% of rows), including Binance, Bybit and OKX: read `rate` and `rate_kind` there.

highest.description: Up to N rows with `rate_8h` ≥ 0, highest first, among fresh rows with a usable interval that clear `min_oi_usd`. Empty when no such row has a rate at or above 0.

lowest.description: Up to N rows with `rate_8h` < 0, lowest first, among the same rows. A rate at or above 0 is never listed here, so this is empty when no eligible rate is below 0.

omitted.description: Rows of the scope left out, each under the first check it failed: `stale` (past the freshness SLA), `no_interval` (no rate or no usable interval), `below_floor` (open interest below `min_oi_usd`, or unknown while the floor is above 0).

symbol.description: The contract that settled. A coin can span several contracts per venue (a USDT and a USDC perp, or PEPE beside 1000PEPE lots), so read series per (exchange, symbol).

funding_apr_mean.description: Mean 8-hour funding over one primary contract per (venue, asset) with a fresh rate, every asset class included (an asset is the funding grid's row: PEPE, 1000PEPE and KPEPE are one asset, so a venue listing two of its spellings counts once), annualized (× 1,095): the computation behind `avg_funding_rate` on GET /v1/market/derivatives-overview, as an APR and without a key. `null` when no contract has a usable rate.

funding_apr_oi_weighted.description: The same, weighted by each contract's one-sided open interest (venues left out of open-interest totals carry no weight). `null` when no contract carries open interest, never the mean in its place.

negative.description: Primary contracts with a fresh rate below 0 (shorts pay longs).

positive.description: Primary contracts with a fresh rate above 0 (longs pay shorts).

complete.description: `coverage_ratio` is at least 0.9; `null` with the ratio. Complete means the span the contract was expected in is covered, not the whole window: with `halted_within_window` or `listed_within_window` true, `acc_*` sums fewer hours than the window (see `covered_hours_*`). Compare `acc_*` across contracts only on complete windows where both of those are false.

halted_within_window.description: The contract stopped trading inside the window: the window is measured up to that halt. The halt is when the instrument master recorded the venue's status leaving trading; when the master has no such time (it first saw the contract already halted), it is the last settlement plus one interval once the contract's current row stopped updating or left the book. `false` when no halt time is known: then the window runs to now and missing settlements read as missing.

listed_within_window.description: The contract's first settlement ever falls inside the window: a short history here is a new listing, not missing data.

meta.description: Which route answered, what the API said about the data's freshness, and whether the client cut the answer to fit the agent's context window.

route.description: Always `v1`: every call reads the keyed /v1 route.

truncated.description: True when the answer is cut short: by the API's row budget, or by the client (`truncated_fields`).

truncated_fields.description: The arrays and strings the client cut, by JSON path in `data`: `total` items received, `showing` kept, `kept: latest` when an oldest-first series kept its newest items.

warnings.description: What the API or the client could not do, in words. State them with the answer.

pagination.description: Present when the answer is one page: pass `cursor` back to read the next one.
